mainTopic: How a חצר acquires (יד, שליחות, moving objects), and whose finds belong to the head of a household, including whether a minor can acquire
overview: The amud opens by wrapping up an earlier discussion. A חצר acquires for its owner because it is like his hand (יד), but it is never weaker than an agent (שליחות). So a gift can be acquired through a person's courtyard when he is absent, but a גט cannot be given that way. Next, רבי יוחנן limits the משנה's rule about running animals to a case where the owner could catch them, and with a gift even that is not needed. רבא then asks whether a house acquires a purse that flies through it and out another door. When challenged from the running animals, he answers that rolling things count as resting, but flying things may not. A new משנה follows: finds of minor children, Canaanite slaves and a wife go to the head of the household, while finds of adult children, Hebrew slaves and a divorced wife belong to the finders. שמואל explains why a minor's find goes to his father. This leads to a debate about whether a minor can acquire by Torah law, using a ברייתא about a worker's son gleaning. אביי's answer is rejected by רב אדא בר מתנה, and the amud ends just as רבא begins a new answer.

steps.title: A courtyard works like a hand, but is no weaker than an agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that חצר comes from the idea of יד, but it also keeps the strengths of שליחות. This explains why a גט and a gift are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: A courtyard was included as a way to acquire because it is like a person's hand, but it is no less effective than an agent. So for a גט, which is a loss for the woman, it does not work when she is absent, because you cannot act against a person's interest unless he is present. For a gift, which is a benefit, it works even when the person is absent, because you can act for a person's benefit even when he is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up its earlier discussion and states the final view on what a חצר is and how it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two models for a חצר: it is like a hand (יד), and it is also like an agent (שליחות). Agency has a known rule: you can do something good for a person without asking him, but not something bad. So a gift (good) can be acquired through his courtyard when he is absent, but a גט (bad for her) cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A courtyard or field that acquires items for its owner
Hand; a חצר works like an extension of the owner's hand
Agency; acting on someone's behalf
Something to a person's detriment
Something to a person's benefit
One may act for a person's benefit even when he is not present

steps.whatToRemember: A חצר is like a hand, but it also has the power of an agent. So it acquires a gift even when the owner is absent, but it cannot receive a גט for a woman who is absent.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not say a חצר is only שליחות or only יד. Its source is יד, and on top of that it is never weaker than שליחות.

phrases.english: A courtyard was included because of 'hand'
phrases.notes: Meaning the תורה's word for 'hand' was read to include a person's courtyard too.

phrases.english: and it is no less than agency.
Regarding a bill of divorce, which is a detriment to her:
one may not act to a person's detriment except in his presence.
Regarding a gift, which is a benefit to him:
one may act for a person's benefit not in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָצֵר אִיתְרַבַּאי מִשּׁוּם יָד וְלָא גָּרְעָה מִשְּׁלִיחוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion (before this section) about whether חצר comes from יד or from שליחות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חצר comes from יד but has at least the power of שליחות. So a גט through her courtyard needs her presence, and a gift through his courtyard works even when he is absent.

steps.title: The field acquires running animals only if he could catch them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה about animals running in a field. רבי יוחנן limits that rule to a case where the field owner could run and catch them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the matter itself. The משנה said: if he saw people running after a found animal and said 'my field has acquired it for me,' it is his. רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is only when he could run after the animals and catch them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה and quotes רבי יוחנן, who adds a condition to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals are still running, so the field cannot really hold them by itself. רבי יוחנן says the field acquires them only if the owner could catch them himself. Then the animals count as being under his control.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself'; returning to discuss a text quoted earlier
A found, ownerless item
And he reaches (catches) them

steps.whyThisMatters: This condition, and the gift question that follows, is exactly what the אמוראים later try to use to answer רבא's question about the flying purse (step 6), though רבא rejects the proof in step 7.

phrases.english: The matter itself.

phrases.aramaic: רָאָה אוֹתָן רָצִין אַחַר הַמְּצִיאָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'If he saw them running after a found item, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: people chase a lost animal, and the field owner says 'my field acquired it for me.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
And that is when he can run after them and catch them.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. רָאָה אוֹתָן רָצִין אַחַר הַמְּצִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by returning to a line from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field acquires running ownerless animals only if the owner could run after them and catch them.

steps.title: What about animals given as a gift?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the same condition applies when the animals are a gift rather than a found item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: with a gift, how does it work?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה raises a question: does the 'he could catch them' condition also apply to a gift?
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a found item, nobody is giving it to him, so the field has to grab it by its own power. With a gift, the owner wants to give it to him, so maybe less is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; raised a question
A gift
How? What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
With a gift, how is it?
phrases.notes: He means animals running in the field that someone is giving him as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether רבי יוחנן's condition from step 2 also applies to a gift.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the field acquire gifted running animals only if he could catch them, or even if he could not?

steps.title: With a gift, the field acquires even if he cannot catch them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר כהנא accepts the answer: with a gift, the field acquires the animals even if the owner could not catch them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר כהנא accepted from him: even if he runs after them and cannot catch them.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. With a gift, the field acquires even without the 'could catch them' condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift is easier to acquire because the giver wants to hand it over. So the field acquires the animals even while they are still running free.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it from him (took this as the answer)
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: A found item needs 'he could catch them.' A gift does not.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana accepted it from him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָץ אַחֲרֵיהֶן וְאֵין מַגִּיעָן.
phrases.english: even though he runs after them and does not catch them.
phrases.notes: The words 'with a gift, the field acquires' are understood here.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: With a gift, the field acquires the running animals even if the owner could not catch them.

steps.title: A purse thrown through a house and out the other door
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a house acquires an object that only passes through its airspace and never lands there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if someone threw a purse in through one doorway and it flew out through another doorway, what is the law? Is an object in the air that will never come to rest there treated as if it is resting, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new case: the purse was inside the house for a moment, but it never landed. Does the house acquire it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חצר normally acquires things that are inside it. Here the purse only passed through the air and kept going out the other side. The question is whether being in the air for a moment, with no landing, counts as being in the חצר.

keyTerms.meaning: A purse or money bag
An entrance or doorway
Airspace
That will not end up coming to rest
Is considered as if it is resting

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If one threw a purse in through this entrance
and it went out through another entrance, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether the house owner acquired it while it flew through his house.

phrases.english: An object in the airspace that will not end up resting
is it considered as resting, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: זָרַק אַרְנָקִי בְּפֶתַח זֶה וְיָצָא בְּפֶתַח אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about a חצר and an object moving through its air.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a חצר acquire an object that passes through its airspace and never comes to rest in it?

steps.title: Isn't this already answered by the משנה about running animals?
steps.stepSummary: An אמורא (רב פפא, or רב אדא בר מתנה, or רבינא) asks רבא why he is asking. The משנה and the gift ruling seem to answer his question already.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא (some say it was רב אדא בר מתנה, some say רבינא): Isn't this the same as our משנה? The משנה says 'if he saw them running after a found item.' רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: only when he could run and catch them. רבי ירמיה asked: how does it work with a gift? And רבי אבא בר כהנא accepted from him: with a gift, the field acquires even if he could not catch them.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רבא's question. He says the case of the running animals already shows the answer, and the גמרא repeats that whole earlier discussion to make the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals running through a field are also not 'resting' in it, yet with a gift the field acquires them even when the owner cannot catch them. So a moving object can be acquired by a חצר, which seems to answer רבא's flying-purse question. The גמרא repeats the earlier lines on purpose, now to use them as the basis for this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (another version of who said it)
Isn't this the same as
Our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The repeated lines are not new rulings. They are the same statements from steps 2 through 4, quoted again as proof for the challenge to רבא.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְרָבָא,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Adda bar Mattana to Rava,
and some say it was Ravina to Rava:
Isn't this the same as our mishna?
'If he saw them running after a found item,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
and that is when he can run after them and catch them,
and Rabbi Yirmeya asked: with a gift, how is it?

phrases.aramaic: וְקַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Abba bar Kahana accepted it from him:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַתָּנָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרָץ אַחֲרֵיהֶן וְאֵין מַגִּיעָן.
phrases.english: with a gift, even though he runs after them and does not catch them.
phrases.notes: This is the key point: the animals never stop moving, and the field still acquires them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's question from step 5, using the discussion from steps 2 through 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about whether airspace that never comes to rest counts as resting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Running animals are also not resting in the field, yet with a gift the field acquires them even when the owner cannot catch them. So the question about a moving object seems already settled.

steps.title: A rolling object is not like a flying one
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the earlier sources dealt with rolling objects, which count as resting on the ground. So they say nothing about an object flying through the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Are you comparing it to something rolling? A rolling object is different, because it counts as if it is resting on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his question. The sources that seemed to answer it were about objects rolling on the ground, not flying through the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An object that rolls touches the ground the whole time, so the field or house can acquire it as if it were lying there. An object flying through the airspace never touches the property at all. So רבא's question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolling. An object moving along the ground.
It is considered as if it is resting in place.
It is different. Used to show that a proof does not fit.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבא, answering the אמורא who challenged him in step 6.

phrases.english: Are you saying "rolling"?
phrases.notes: רבא means: your proof is about something rolling on the ground, but I asked about something flying through the air.

phrases.english: Rolling is different,
since it is like something resting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by showing that its sources do not fit רבא's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger thought the earlier rulings about animals or objects in a field already settled the airspace question.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rolling object counts as resting on the ground, so those rulings do not decide the case of an object that only passes through the air.
steps.whatToRemember: An object rolling on the ground counts as if it is resting there. An object flying through the air is still an open question.

steps.title: Whose finds belong to the head of the household
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that finds of minor children, Canaanite slaves and a wife belong to the head of the household. Finds of adult children, Hebrew slaves and a divorced wife belong to the finders.
steps.simpleTranslation: The found item of his minor son or daughter, of his Canaanite slave or maidservant, and of his wife: these belong to him. The found item of his adult son or daughter, of his Hebrew slave or maidservant, and of his wife whom he divorced, even if he has not yet paid her כתובה: these belong to them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sorts the people in a man's household into two lists: those whose finds go to him, and those who keep their own finds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list is minors, Canaanite slaves and a wife. The second list is people who are not under him in the same way: adult children, Hebrew slaves, and a divorced wife. Even if he still owes the divorced wife her כתובה, her finds are her own.

keyTerms.meaning: A found item. Something ownerless that a person picks up.
Minors. Children below the age of adulthood.
Canaanite slave. Owned fully by his master.
Hebrew slave. A Jew working for a set term, who keeps his own finds.
The payment a husband owes his wife when he divorces her.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The found item of his minor son and daughter,
the found item of his Canaanite slave and maidservant,
the found item of his wife:
these are his.
The found item of his adult son and daughter,
the found item of his Hebrew slave and maidservant,
the found item of his wife whom he divorced,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן כְּתוּבָּה –
phrases.english: even though he has not given the כתובה:
these are theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the airspace discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Finds of minor children, Canaanite slaves and a wife belong to the head of the household. Finds of adult children, Hebrew slaves and a divorced wife belong to the finders.
steps.confusionAlert: The divorced wife keeps her finds even if the husband has not paid her כתובה yet. Don't think the unpaid debt keeps her tied to him for this purpose.

steps.title: שמואל explains why a minor's find goes to the father
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says a minor's find belongs to the father because a child who finds something runs right to his father with it and does not keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Why did the חכמים say a minor's find belongs to his father? Because when he finds it, he runs with it to his father and does not keep it in his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with שמואל explaining the reason behind the first ruling of the משנה about a minor's find.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gives a practical reason: children naturally bring what they find to their father. It is not because the father owns the child. This reason will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor child.
He runs with it.
He does not keep it in his hand.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel said:
For what reason did they say
that a minor's found item goes to his father?
Because at the time he finds it,
he runs with it to his father,
and does not keep it in his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ מְצִיאַת קָטָן לְאָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the משנה's ruling about a minor's find.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor's find goes to his father because the child naturally brings it straight to him.

steps.title: Can a minor acquire for himself? A ברייתא about gleaning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל means a minor cannot acquire anything for himself by Torah law. It brings a ברייתא about a worker's son gleaning in the field, which שמואל rules is the halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean שמואל holds that a minor cannot acquire for himself by Torah law? But a ברייתא teaches: If someone hires a worker, the worker's son may glean behind him. If the worker gets half, a third or a quarter of the crop, his son may not glean behind him. רבי יוסי says: Either way, his son and wife may glean behind him. And שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge to שמואל. It brings a ברייתא and שמואל's ruling on it. The next step spells out the full point of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's reason sounds like a minor cannot own what he finds, so it goes to his father. But in the ברייתא, רבי יוסי lets the son glean even when his father is a partner in the crop, and שמואל rules like רבי יוסי. This seems to treat the son's gleanings as his own, so the גמרא is preparing to show a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquiring. Gaining legal ownership of something.
By Torah law.
May glean. Pick up fallen stalks that the Torah leaves for the poor.
A hired worker.
Either way. In both cases.

phrases.english: Is this to say that Shmuel holds
that a minor cannot acquire for himself
by Torah law?
But it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who hires a worker:
his son may glean behind him.
phrases.notes: Gleaning means picking up the stalks that fall during harvest. The תורה leaves these for poor people.

phrases.english: If for half, a third or a quarter:
phrases.notes: Here the worker is paid with a share of the crop, so he is partly an owner of the field.

phrases.english: his son may not glean behind him.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Either way,
his son and wife may glean behind him.
And Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל קָטָן לֵית לֵיהּ זְכִיָּיה לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what שמואל's reason implies and sets it against a ruling שמואל himself accepts.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea, drawn from שמואל's reason, that a minor cannot acquire for himself by Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules like רבי יוסי that the worker's son may glean even when his father shares in the crop. That seems to assume the son's gleanings belong to the son. If a minor could not acquire for himself, this ruling would be hard to explain.
steps.whyThisMatters: Whether a minor can own things by Torah law affects many areas of הלכה. Here it decides whether a child's find belongs to him or to his father.

steps.title: Why may the worker's son glean if he gleans for his wealthy father?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא. If a minor cannot acquire for himself, his gleanings belong to his father. The father does not count as poor, so the son should not be allowed to glean.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works if you say a minor can acquire for himself: he gleans for himself, and then his father acquires it from him. But if a minor cannot acquire for himself, he is gleaning for his father. His father counts as wealthy, so why may his wife and son glean after him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the attack it began in step 10. It shows exactly why the ברייתא about the worker's son seems to contradict the idea that a minor cannot acquire for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gleanings in the field may only be taken by poor people. If the son can acquire for himself, he is a poor person who owns nothing, so he gleans legally and only afterward hands it to his father. If he cannot acquire, the stalks go straight to the father, who is not poor, and the ברייתא's permission makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: The ability to acquire something for oneself
Gleans, meaning he picks up the fallen stalks left for the poor
Wealthy, meaning not counted as poor for gifts to the poor
It works well if you say..., the opening of a 'this fits, but that does not' argument

steps.confusionAlert: The father here is not truly rich. He counts as 'wealthy' only because, as a worker, he has a share in the crop, so he is not a poor person who may glean.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that a minor can acquire for himself,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מְלַקֵּט – לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ קָא מְלַקֵּט,
phrases.english: then when he gleans, he gleans for himself,
and his father acquires it from him afterward.
But if you say
that a minor cannot acquire for himself,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מְלַקֵּט – לְאָבִיו קָא מְלַקֵּט,
phrases.english: then when he gleans, he gleans for his father,
and his father is wealthy,
phrases.notes: He means the father has a share in the crop as a worker, so he doesn't count as poor.

phrases.english: so why may his wife and son glean after him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא קָטָן אִית לֵיהּ זְכִיָּיה לְנַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge introduced in step 10 by explaining the logic of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reasoning in step 9, which implies that a minor cannot acquire for himself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows the son to glean, which only works if he acquires for himself first. שמואל rules like that ברייתא, so his own reasoning seems to contradict it.

steps.title: שמואל only explained our משנה's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל was giving the reasoning of the תנא of our משנה, but he himself does not agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל was saying the reason of our תנא, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל's explanation in step 9 was only a description of how our משנה thinks, not his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives a minor's find to his father, which fits the view that a minor cannot acquire. שמואל explained that view, but in his own opinion a minor can acquire for himself. That is why he can rule like the ברייתא about the gleaning son.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason of our תנא, meaning the author of our משנה
He does not hold that way himself

phrases.english: שמואל was stating the reason of our תנא,
phrases.notes: 'Our תנא' is the author of the משנה about a minor's find, from step 8.

phrases.english: but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reattribution: the statement explains someone else's view, not the speaker's own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל personally held that a minor cannot acquire for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל was only explaining our משנה. He himself holds that a minor can acquire, so ruling like the ברייתא fits his view.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really hold that a minor acquires by Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the view that a minor acquires for himself, which it links with רבי יוסי, is really a Torah-law view. It quotes a משנה where רבי יוסי calls taking a minor's find 'full robbery'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי hold that a minor can acquire by Torah law? But we learned in a משנה: taking the find of a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor counts as robbery because of the ways of peace. רבי יוסי says: it is full robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the view שמואל follows means a minor acquires by Torah law. It brings a משנה from גיטין as the source for its question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה says taking a minor's find is robbery only as a rabbinic rule, for the sake of peace. רבי יוסי says it is 'full robbery', which at first sounds like Torah-level ownership. The next step will show that even this is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
But didn't we learn in a משנה, which introduces a source for a challenge
A deaf-mute, a mentally incompetent person and a minor, who are not legally competent
The ways of peace, a rabbinic reason to keep people from fighting
Full robbery

phrases.english: And does רבי יוסי hold
that a minor can acquire by Torah law?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The find of a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor:
taking it from them counts as robbery
because of the ways of peace.
רבי יוסי says: it is full robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי קָטָן אִית לֵיהּ זְכִיָּיה מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12 by asking whether רבי יוסי's view really means a minor acquires by Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל follows a view in which a minor acquires for himself by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי יוסי treats a minor's find as protected only by rabbinic law, then he does not hold that a minor acquires by Torah law. That leaves the gleaning problem unsolved.

steps.title: רב חסדא: 'full robbery' only by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רבי יוסי means full robbery by rabbinic law. The only practical difference is that judges can force the item to be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: it is full robbery by rabbinic law. The practical difference is that judges can take it back from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חסדא's explanation to complete its challenge. It shows that even רבי יוסי does not hold that a minor acquires by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's 'full robbery' is still a rabbinic rule. He differs from the first opinion only in that the court may force the item back. So even according to רבי יוסי, a minor does not acquire by Torah law, and the challenge stands until אביי answers it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: By their words, meaning by rabbinic law
The practical difference that results
To have it taken back through the judges, meaning by court order

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי יוסי's 'full robbery' is only rabbinic. The court can force the item back, but a minor still does not acquire by Torah law. So the גמרא needs a new reason why רבי יוסי lets the son glean, and אביי gives one in the next step.

phrases.english: And רב חסדא said:
It is full robbery by rabbinic law.
The practical difference is
to have it taken out of his hands by the judges.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גָּזֵל גָּמוּר מִדִּבְרֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge of step 13 by explaining רבי יוסי's words as rabbinic.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי does not hold that a minor acquires by Torah law
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's explanation of רבי יוסי in the משנה in גיטין

steps.title: אביי: The poor give up on the field, so anyone may glean
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the worker's son may glean because the poor people themselves give up on this field. That makes it like a field already gone over by the last gleaners, where even the non-poor may take what is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: The חכמים treated this field like one the last gleaners have already walked through. The poor people themselves stop thinking about it, because they assume, 'That man's son is gleaning it for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new answer to the question of how a worker's son may glean, even if a minor cannot acquire for himself by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the last poor gleaners have passed through a field, the leftover stalks are open to everyone, even the rich. אביי says that when the poor see the worker's son gleaning, they give up on the field. So the field counts as already finished by the poor. The son's gleanings then go to his father with no problem, even though the father is not poor.

keyTerms.meaning: The last stragglers, meaning the final poor people who glean. After them anyone may take what remains.
Gleanings, the fallen stalks left for the poor.
They take their minds off it, meaning they give up hope of getting it.
Poor people

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
They made it like a field through which the last gleaners have walked.
For the poor people themselves put it out of their minds.
They think: that man's son is gleaning it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 13 and 14 showed that even רבי יוסי holds a minor cannot acquire by Torah law, so the son's gleanings go straight to his father. אביי offers a new reason why רבי יוסי still lets the son glean.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning: the field's status changes because the poor give up on it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son should not glean, because his gleanings would go to his father, who is not poor.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poor give up on the field, so it counts as finished by the last gleaners, and anyone may glean there.

steps.title: רב אדא: You may not drive the poor away, like setting a lion in your field
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה challenges אביי. Letting the son glean so the poor give up is like keeping a lion in your field to scare the poor off, and that cannot be allowed. So the גמרא turns to רבא for a different answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said to אביי: Is a person allowed to have a lion crouch in his field so that the poor will see it and run away? Rather, רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה knocks down אביי's answer. The last words, 'Rather, רבא said,' set up a new answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer depends on the poor giving up because of the son. רב אדא בר מתנה argues that causing the poor to leave is itself wrong, just like scaring them off with a lion. A rule cannot be built on driving the poor away, so אביי's explanation falls.

keyTerms.meaning: To make crouch or lie down
A lion
And they will flee
But is it allowed? A question that means it is clearly not allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said to Abaye:
But is a person permitted
to have a lion crouch in his field
phrases.notes: He is comparing the gleaning son to a lion. Both scare off the poor so they do not take what is theirs.

phrases.english: so that the poor will see it and flee?
Rather, Rava said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה לְאַבָּיֵי וְכִי מוּתָּר לָאָדָם
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the field is like one finished by the last gleaners, because the poor give up on it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The poor only give up because the son drives them away. Driving away the poor is forbidden, like setting a lion in your field. So this cannot be the reason the son may glean.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אדא is not saying the poor do not give up. He agrees they do. His point is that causing them to give up is not allowed, so it cannot make the son's gleaning permitted.
